title: World Liberty Financial founding and token sale
summary: WLF launched on 16 Sept 2024, seven weeks before the election, with Trump family backing. It had issued only the WLFI governance token and the USD1 stablecoin until its first app, World Liberty Markets, went live on 12 Jan 2026. Chase Herro's 2018 'sh*t in a can' rant is real, and October 2024 sales were poor enough that the target was cut 90% to $30M. The claim compresses the timeline: sales barely moved after the election, recovered only after Justin Sun's $30M buy on 25 Nov 2024, sold out the first tranche around 20 Jan 2025, and reached $550M in March 2025.

sub_claims.statement: WLF was created by the Trump family shortly before the 2024 election.
sub_claims.finding: Launched on 16 Sept 2024 in an X Spaces event and announced by Trump. The operating founders were Chase Herro and Zachary Folkman, with Donald Trump, Eric Trump and Donald Trump Jr. backing them. Trump-owned DT Marks DEFI LLC is entitled to 75% of net protocol revenue.

sub_claims.statement: WLF has launched only the WLFI governance token and USD1 stablecoin, with no DeFi application yet.
sub_claims.finding: True until January 2026. The WLFI sale opened on 15 Oct 2024, USD1 was confirmed in March 2025 with BitGo as custodian, and WLFI began trading on 1 Sept 2025. The claim is now outdated: the lending app World Liberty Markets, built on Dolomite, launched on 12 Jan 2026.

sub_claims.statement: Co-founder Chase Herro said you can sell 'sh*t in a can ... covered in human skin for a billion dollars if the story's right'.
sub_claims.finding: From a 2018 YouTube video, since made private and aired by MSNBC in 2024. The full quote includes 'wrapped in piss'. Herro has called himself the 'dirtbag of the internet'. In Nov 2025 WLF promoted a memecoin named after the rant ($SPSC).

sub_claims.statement: In October 2024 token sales were bad.
sub_claims.finding: The target was $300M (20B tokens at $0.015, a $1.5B valuation). About 4% of that sold on day one, and an SEC filing on 30 Oct 2024 cut the goal to $30M. The explanation that 'some thought Trump might lose' is speculation. Reported causes were the accredited-investor-only structure, technical problems and weak demand.

sub_claims.statement: As Trump won, WLF sales exploded and sold out $550 million.
sub_claims.finding: No post-election bump: under $1,500 sold in the 24 hours after the win, with $14.8M to $15.4M cumulative. Sales jumped after Justin Sun's $30M purchase on 25 Nov 2024, which brought the total to about $52M. The first tranche ($300M) sold out around 20 Jan 2025, after the $TRUMP and $MELANIA memecoin launches. A second tranche (5B tokens at $0.05) raised $250M, bringing the total to $550M by about 14 March 2025.

corrections: Claimed: Sales 'exploded' as Trump won. The record shows: almost no sales right after the election, and the rebound followed Justin Sun's $30M buy on 25 Nov 2024.

Claimed: WLF 'sold out $550 million worth' around the election. The record shows: the first $300M tranche sold out around 20 Jan 2025 and the $550M total was reached in March 2025 after a second, higher-priced tranche.
Claimed: No application has launched. The record shows: World Liberty Markets (lending) launched on 12 Jan 2026.
Claimed: WLF was 'created by the Trump family'. The record shows: the named founders are Chase Herro and Zak Folkman, with the Trump family as promoters and revenue recipients via DT Marks DEFI LLC.
The co-founder's name is Chase Herro, sometimes misspelled 'Chase Hero'.
denials_and_context: WLF presents its $550M raise as a success; Folkman credited Sun's investment with reviving the project.
WLF has not disputed the Herro video and later embraced the meme by promoting the SPSC memecoin.
The public sale excluded US retail (accredited investors only), which limited early demand regardless of election odds.
WLF also sold additional WLFI privately, outside the public $550M figure.
